summary.text: Pete Sessions is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to Texas's 17th District. A Waco native who spent 16 years at Southwestern Bell Telephone Company, he was first elected to Congress in 1996, chaired the House Rules Committee from 2013 to 2019, and returned to the House in 2021 after losing in 2018. He chairs the Government Operations Subcommittee of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee.

paragraphs.text: Sessions was born in Waco, Texas, in 1955, and attended local public schools through ninth grade before moving to Winston Churchill High School in San Antonio.
He earned a B.S. from Southwestern University in 1978 and later spent twelve years on the university's Board of Trustees.
He worked 16 years for Southwestern Bell Telephone Company, retiring as District Manager, according to his official biography; Ballotpedia describes his career as working as an executive with AT&T.
His father, William Sessions, was a federal district judge and the fourth Director of the FBI, appointed by President Ronald Reagan.

Sessions was first elected to Congress in 1996, and his official biography says he spent a decade in House Republican leadership and chaired the National Republican Congressional Committee from 2009 through 2012.
He chaired the House Committee on Rules from 2013 to 2019.

He lost the November 2018 general election in Texas's 32nd District to Democrat Colin Allred, then won the Republican nomination and the November 3, 2020 general election in the 17th District, defeating Democrat Rick Kennedy and Libertarian Ted Brown.
His official biography credits Sessions with sponsoring the Family Opportunity Act of 2005 (enacted 2006) and the Border Tunnel Task Force Act (passed 2018).
In the 119th Congress he chairs the Government Operations Subcommittee of the Oversight and Government Reform Committee and sits on the Financial Services Committee.

According to his official biography, he, his father and two of his sons are Eagle Scouts, and he has held leadership roles with the Boy Scouts of America; he lives in Waco with his wife, Karen, and they have five sons.
